paper_metadata.title: An Empirical Study on Enhancing Explainability through Quantum Machine Learning for Credit Risk Analysis

experiments.description: Quantum support vector classification of credit score classes using a ZZFeatureMap quantum kernel.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical credit features are encoded into a quantum feature map; the paper does not specify qubit-to-feature mapping beyond use of the ZZFeatureMap.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Credit score classification via maximum-margin separation in quantum feature space.

problem_instance.description: Credit score classification on a dataset with age, gender, income, education, marital status, number of children, home ownership, and credit score.

dataset_specification.description: Kaggle credit score classification dataset; categorical variables label-encoded; numerical features standardized; train/test split used, but exact ratio not reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Label encoding of categorical variables; standard scaling of numerical features; train/test split; optional KPCA mentioned in the overall pipeline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Test accuracy evaluation; LIME-based feature importance analysis.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims quantum methods may improve accuracy and efficiency, but no explicit speedup factor or runtime comparison is reported for the ZZFeatureMap experiment.

experiments.description: Quantum support vector classification of credit score classes using a PauliFeatureMap quantum kernel.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical credit features are encoded into a quantum feature map using single-qubit rotations around Pauli axes.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Credit score classification via maximum-margin separation in quantum feature space.

problem_instance.description: Credit score classification on the same public benchmark dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Kaggle credit score classification dataset; categorical variables label-encoded; numerical features standardized; train/test split used, but exact ratio not reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Label encoding of categorical variables; standard scaling of numerical features; train/test split; optional KPCA mentioned in the overall pipeline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Test accuracy evaluation; LIME-based feature importance analysis.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit runtime, computational cost, or asymptotic speedup is reported for the PauliFeatureMap experiment.

experiments.description: Quantum support vector classification of credit score classes using a combined ZZPauliMap quantum feature map.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Stratified k-fold cross-validation and grid search used for evaluation/optimization; exact stopping rule not reported.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical credit features are encoded using multi-axis single-qubit rotations and ZZ entangling gates across qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Credit score classification via maximum-margin separation in quantum feature space.

problem_instance.description: Credit score classification on the same public benchmark dataset, evaluated with a hybrid quantum feature map.

dataset_specification.description: Kaggle credit score classification dataset; categorical variables label-encoded; numerical features standardized; stratified k-fold cross-validation and grid search applied; exact k and train/test split not reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Label encoding of categorical variables; standard scaling of numerical features; train/test split; optional KPCA mentioned in the overall pipeline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Test accuracy evaluation; LIME-based feature importance analysis.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports improved classification accuracy for the combined ZZPauliMap, but does not provide a measured speedup, training time, or complexity-based advantage over the classical baseline.
